title: Choosing the Right Model for Your Project
excerpt: Not all models are the same. Here is how to pick the best one for your use case and budget.

content.h: Match the model to the job 🎯

content.p: Small, fast models are perfect for classification, extraction and simple chat. Large reasoning models shine at complex analysis and code.

content.caption: Speed vs capability for each class of task

content.p: Credits are consumed based on the number of input and output tokens. A cheaper model can often achieve the same result when the task is simple.
Run a few representative prompts through a small model first. If quality is not enough, move up the model ladder instead of paying for the largest one from day one.
Check your usage regularly in the panel and switch models if you see a big gap between quality and spend.

faq.a: The mini-class models have the lowest latency and are best for chat, extraction and classification.

faq.q: When should I pay for a reasoning model?
faq.a: For math, code and multi-step analysis, reasoning models are usually worth the extra cost.
Yes. Tokens are model-agnostic — just change the model name in your request.

faq.q: Do all models cost the same?
faq.a: No. Each model class has its own credit price, shown in the panel before you send.
